newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien reappoints Canada finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Chretien reappoints Canada finance minister.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien has reappointed fiscally conservative Paul Martin as finance minister, Chretien spokesman Peter Donolo said on Wednesday.
"The economic team is totally unchanged," Donolo told Reuters before the cabinet swearing-in ceremony.
He cited the reappointment of Martin as well as Industry Minister John Manley and Treasury Board President Marcel Masse.
"I think it's a very strong message about direction, about continuity, about seeing through the plan," Donolo said.
Martin won international praise in the Liberals' first term for slashing the Canadian budget deficit.

Donolo also confirmed that Sheila Copps, one of the left-leaning members of the cabinet, would relinquish her post as deputy prime minister. He attributed that to the fact that the Liberal majority was now slimmer and required closer management. The new deputy prime minister, Herb Gray, was House leader in the last parliament.
The full cabinet list is to be released at 1100 EDT (1500 GMT).
